answer: Each identity locks a 90-credit bond and draws a fresh task from a cedar board; the crystal draw never repeats one. The identity completes it and files a key-signed proof; auditors replay it publicly. Anyone who tries to forge a proof fails replay; the bond burns. Repeat filings cost more: the k-th identity pays 42+11(k-1); 1,000 fakes pay 5,536,500 plus 90,000 locked, above a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 42 once and keep the bond.
